params.script_inline:
import sys, json, datetime

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
phase = str(ctx.get("ses_phase", ""))
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
# `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked, and
# both have to be read (GH #343).
err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
# The channel is the identity a session belongs to. The ingress edge promotes
# it (a chat id, a room, a phone number); a colony with a single surface can
# leave it unset and run on one generation line.
channel = str(ctx.get("channel", "") or hop.get("channel", "") or "default")
# The round the generation is opened in. It is DECLARED at the door a turn
# enters by -- one talky serves one round, and a change of the round ends the
# generation (ADR-0002 E8) -- so it is a constant of this generation and the
# opening turn is the only place it can be recorded. Never derived from the
# session_id prefix, and never invented: a door that declares nothing leaves
# the column empty, and a consumer that needs a round refuses that batch
# rather than writing a row that claims everyone was present.
#
# E8 is enforced HERE since GH #940 (PP-S3-2): a turn whose round differs from
# the open generation of its channel SEALS that generation -- with the round it
# was opened in -- and opens a new one. Up to session-keeper 2.2.2 the round was
# only written at the opening, so a generation opened in round A went on taking
# the turns of round B, and its close pass handed both rounds' turns over under
# A: the episodes of B were filed for people who were not there.
audience = str(ctx.get("audience_set", "") or "")


def canonical_round(value):
    """The round as one comparable string, normalised exactly as the close pass
    groups it (memory-hive close-glue `canon`, GH #933): a JSON list of
    participant ids, deduplicated, blanks dropped, sorted, compact -- so
    `["a","b"]` and `["b", "a"]` are one round. An empty list is NO round ("")
    there and therefore here, or a row opened in `[]` and a round-less turn
    would be two rounds to this cell and one to the close pass. A value that is
    not such a list is compared as it stands."""
    raw = str(value or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return ""
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(raw)
    except Exception:
        return raw
    if isinstance(parsed, list) and all(isinstance(p, str) for p in parsed):
        items = sorted({p.strip() for p in parsed if p.strip()})
        return json.dumps(items, separators=(",", ":")) if items else ""
    return raw


ROUND = canonical_round(audience)
# THE TURN'S OWN ID (display-hive.md 2 / 8.2), carried untouched when the
# channel assigned one on acceptance -- and minted at `in_turn` below only for
# a turn that came without (GH #953, R-1). This cell adds the session id and
# hands the turn on. It used to build the outgoing `turn` header from scratch and copy
# only the BODY into it, so the id died at the stamp -- measured 2026-09-18 on
# the live colonies, spoken and typed. Context first, hop second, like `channel`
# above and for the same reason: the session lookup in between answers under the
# STORE's hop. Empty stays empty.
turn_id = str(ctx.get("turn_id", "") or hop.get("turn_id", "") or "")
FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
now_dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
now = now_dt.strftime(FMT)


# What a turn leaves on its generation's `owed_turn` (GH #953): the turn id it
# carries -- the channel's, or the one this door minted for a turn that came
# without (`in_turn` below). '*' is only the fallback of a store reply that
# carries no id at all (a lookup in flight across the upgrade); an answer
# without an id acknowledges exactly that mark. Never '' -- that is "nothing
# owed", and a seal would close at once.
OWED = turn_id or "*"


def seal_stamp(i):
    """The `closed_at` of the i-th generation this run seals: `now` plus i
    microseconds. WHY (GH #954, review I-1): the unique index
    `sessions_open_round` is (channel, audience_set, closed_at), and a run that
    sealed two generations of one round with the SAME `now` wrote two rows the
    index cannot hold -- the next wake then fails to create it and the claim
    of the round is gone. One run, one distinct stamp per sealed row."""
    return (now_dt + datetime.timedelta(microseconds=i)).strftime(FMT)


COLUMNS = ["channel", "session_id", "opened_at", "last_seen", "closed", "closed_at",
           "audience_set", "owed_turn"]
# How many open generations of ONE channel a lookup reads. Since GH #940 a
# channel holds at most one open generation per round, and every turn of a new
# round seals the others, so more than a handful only appear after a refused
# seal or two turns of a new round in the same instant; a row past the bound
# is left to the night sweep, which closes it under its own round.
OPEN_LIMIT = 16


def park():
    """Terminal by design. The stamp sits in the ingress path of a loop:
    anything it cannot name is parked rather than answered."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def store_op(args, ph, session="", keep="", old_round=""):
    """Every emission carries the full key set the hive edges read. A missing
    hop key makes a CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge --
    so keys are always present and empty rather than absent. `audience_set` is
    the round of the generation a `seal` ends (GH #940): it rides the store
    round trip as `context.keeper_audience`, because the store answers rows
    and not the round that asked."""
    return {"header": {"route": "kstore", "phase": ph, "channel": channel,
                       "session_id": session, "keeper_body": keep,
                       "turn_id": turn_id, "audience_set": old_round},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "k-" + ph,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def store_bundle(legs, ph, session="", keep="", old_round=""):
    """ONE store message with one `tool_call` turn per leg (GH #295): the store
    runs the legs one after the other in ONE handle and answers with ONE
    message -- `hop.operation` 'bundle', a `tool_result` per leg in
    `messages[]` and the per-leg metadata in `results[]`, both tied to the leg
    by its `tool_call_id`. The same full hop key set as `store_op`."""
    msg = store_op({}, ph, session, keep, old_round)
    msg["messages"] = [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": lid,
                        "text": json.dumps(args)} for lid, args in legs]
    return msg


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        rows = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []


def leg_result(doc, lid):
    """The `results[]` entry of one bundle leg, {} when the reply has none."""
    for r in doc.get("results") or []:
        if isinstance(r, dict) and str(r.get("tool_call_id") or "") == lid:
            return r
    return {}


def leg_rows(doc, lid):
    """The rows a `select` leg of a bundle returned, read off ITS tool_result
    turn (matched by id, never by position)."""
    for m in doc.get("messages") or []:
        if isinstance(m, dict) and str(m.get("id") or "") == lid:
            try:
                rows = json.loads(m.get("text", "[]"))
            except Exception:
                return []
            return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []
    return []


def leg_error(doc, ids):
    """(leg id, error_code) of the first leg among `ids` that the store
    refused, or None. A bundle never refuses wholesale for one leg: the header
    `error_code` stays empty and the refusal sits on the leg (GH #295)."""
    for lid in ids:
        code = str(leg_result(doc, lid).get("error_code") or "")
        if code:
            return lid, code
    return None


def seal_legs(rsid, stamp):
    """The seal of one generation as two guarded legs (GH #953). `seal-done`
    takes a generation that owes no answer (`owed_turn` empty, or NULL on a
    row from before the column) and clears the mark with it; `seal-owed`
    takes one whose last turn is still waiting for its final answer and leaves
    the mark standing, so the answer's acknowledgement (`in_answered`) sends
    the close. Both are guarded by `closed = 0`: at most one of them flips a
    row, and neither does when somebody sealed it first."""
    return [("seal-done", {"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                           "set": {"closed": 1, "closed_at": stamp, "owed_turn": ""},
                           "where": {"session_id": rsid, "closed": 0,
                                     "owed_turn": {"or_null": {"eq": ""}}}}),
            ("seal-owed", {"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                           "set": {"closed": 1, "closed_at": stamp},
                           "where": {"session_id": rsid, "closed": 0}})]


def refused(ph, opname, code, state):
    """The reject of this cell: hop.reject_reason 'store_refused', the store's
    own code and the refused op, and a body that says what is still true."""
    return {"header": {"route": "reject", "reject_reason": "store_refused",
                       "store_error": code, "store_operation": str(opname),
                       "phase": "", "channel": channel, "session_id": "",
                       "turn_id": turn_id,
                       "keeper_body": ""},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "k-reject",
                          "text": "the session store refused the " + str(opname)
                                  + " of step '" + ph + "': " + code + ". "
                                  + state}]}


def close_of(session, room, round_):
    """The close of one generation: the same shape the night sends."""
    return {"header": {"route": "close", "phase": "", "channel": room,
                       "session_id": session, "audience_set": round_},
            "messages": []}


SEAL_REFUSED = ("the turn was ALREADY stamped and handed on in a generation of "
                "its own round; only the generation of the previous round was "
                "not sealed, so it stays open until the night sweep closes it "
                "-- under its own round, never under the new one")
ACK_REFUSED = ("the final answer of the turn was already written; only its "
               "acknowledgement did not take, so a generation sealed while it "
               "waited for that answer keeps its mark and no close is sent now "
               "-- the night releases the mark and closes it once the channel "
               "has been silent past the idle threshold")


def held_turn(sid):
    """The turn this keeper held back while its generation was being opened
    (GH #954): its body rode the store round trip as `keeper_body`."""
    try:
        keep = json.loads(str(ctx.get("keeper_body", "") or "{}"))
    except Exception:
        keep = {}
    if not isinstance(keep, dict):
        keep = {}
    keep.setdefault("messages", [])
    turn = {"header": {"route": "turn", "phase": "", "channel": channel,
                       "session_id": sid, "turn_id": turn_id}}
    turn.update(keep)
    return turn


def look(body_text):
    """Every open generation of the channel, the turn riding along."""
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "sessions", "columns": COLUMNS,
                     "where": {"channel": channel, "closed": 0},
                     "order_by": [{"col": "opened_at", "dir": "desc"}],
                     "limit": OPEN_LIMIT},
                    "look", "", body_text)


# ================================================================== CLAIMED
# GH #954: two first turns of a round that has no open generation both look
# before either opens one. Measured on a real colony (20 of 20 runs): both
# opened a generation of the SAME round, the round's conversation was split
# over two closes, and one of the two racing turns reached neither close
# batch whole. The open is therefore a claim: the unique index
# `sessions_open_round` on (channel, audience_set, closed_at) lets one open
# generation of a round stand per channel -- an open row's `closed_at` is
# empty -- and the turn waits for its own insert. The loser of the race meets
# the index and looks again: it finds the winner's generation and runs in it.
if err == "unique_violation" and op == "insert" and phase == "open":
    emit([look(str(ctx.get("keeper_body", "") or "{}"))])

# ================================================================== REFUSED
# A store refusal is not a result, and it sits AHEAD of the lanes and the
# phases. Measured before the guard existed: a refused `look` came back as an
# empty row list, the lazy-reopen branch below read that as "this channel has
# no open session", and OPENED A SECOND GENERATION for a channel that already
# had one. Two sessions, two close batches, one history split down the middle
# -- and nothing said a word. "The store did not answer" and "there is no row"
# are not the same sentence, and only one of them may open a generation.
#
# What is still true after the refusal differs per step, and the text says
# which step this was. `look` is the only one that still owes the turn: `touch`
# and `open` are fire-and-forget, they ride in the SAME emission as the stamped
# turn, so by the time their refusal arrives the turn is already downstream.
# Claiming "the turn was NOT stamped" there would be the opposite of the truth.
if err and op:
    if phase == "seal":
        state = SEAL_REFUSED
    elif phase == "ack":
        state = ACK_REFUSED
    elif phase == "open":
        state = ("the turn was ALREADY stamped and handed on beside this refusal, carrying "
                 "session id '" + str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or "") + "', "
                 "whose ROW was never written. The next turn on this channel finds "
                 "no open session and opens ANOTHER generation under a different "
                 "id, so this turn ends up alone in a session nothing else "
                 "joins")
    elif phase == "touch":
        state = ("the turn was ALREADY stamped and handed on; only the idle "
                 "clock was not restarted, so the night may end this generation "
                 "early even though somebody was still talking")
    else:
        state = ("the turn was NOT stamped and no generation was opened -- an "
                 "unanswered lookup is not a channel without a session, and a "
                 "turn that travels without a session id is worse than a turn "
                 "that stops here")
    out = []
    if phase == "open":
        # The turn waited for its open (GH #954); a refusal other than the
        # claim's does not stop it -- the conversation goes on, as before.
        out.append(held_turn(str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or "")))
    emit(out + [refused(phase, op, err, state)])

# ==================================================================== LANES
if lane == "in_turn":
    if op is not None:
        park()
    # A turn WITHOUT a channel id gets one here, at the door of the keeper
    # (GH #953, Re-Review R-1). Measured on the Telegram road: its text turns
    # carry no id, so up to Fix-Runde 1 every one of them owed its answer
    # under the single mark '*', and the answer to an EARLIER turn
    # acknowledged the debt of a later one -- a double message followed by a
    # round change sealed the generation as owing nothing and closed it before
    # the answer to the second message stood on the wall (#953 again, lock
    # `gh953 ... a_double_message_without_ids_closes_after_the_answer_to_the_last_turn`).
    # The id is the substrate's trace of this turn (a channel's inbound
    # message is a source message, its own trace) plus this instant, so two
    # turns of one trace stay two marks. The keeper's store edge promotes it to `context.turn_id`,
    # the turn leaves with it, and the answer brings it back on `turn_write`.
    # A channel id is carried untouched.
    if not turn_id:
        turn_id = "keeper:" + str(envelope.get("trace_id", "") or "") + ":" + now
    # The turn rides through the lookup on the hop: a store reply carries the
    # row, not the conversation that asked for it. EVERY open generation of the
    # channel, not the newest one: the decision below compares each one's round
    # with this turn's (GH #940), and a round compared on one row only would
    # leave a second open one of another round behind unsealed.
    emit([look(json.dumps(d))])

# ================================================================ ANSWERED
# GH #953 (review I-3, OR-NL-163): the ORDER of a close is an EVENT, not a
# path length. A turn of a new round seals the open generation of the old one,
# and the last answer of that generation's last turn reaches the wall on its
# own branch (brain -> curator in_llm -> intake -> ledger bundle). Up to here
# the close was sent at the seal, and the answer arrived first only because
# its branch happened to be shorter: the builder's measurement, 0 of 20 runs
# lost with a lead of 47-65 deliveries, is a probability and not an order.
#
# The event is this lane. `./curator/intake` emits the answer's insert bundle
# to its ledger and, IN THE SAME EMISSION, the episode to `./writer`, which
# turns it into `turn_write` -- so anything that leaves causally AFTER a
# `turn_write` stands behind that insert in the ledger's FIFO. The parent
# wires `turn_write` here as `in_answered`; a turn sets `owed_turn` to its
# channel turn id (touch / open), a seal of a generation that still owes an
# answer (`seal-owed`) sends NO close, and the acknowledgement of that answer
# clears the mark and sends it -- after the answer is on the wall. Only the
# FINAL answer acknowledges (origin 'assistant'); the person's own turn and a
# peer's travel the same lane and are parked. The turn id is the CHANNEL's
# (`context.turn_id`), never `hop.turn_id`, which on `turn_write` is the
# episode id `<session>#<tag>-<index>`. An answer with an id clears its own
# turn's mark or an id-less one ('*'); an answer without an id clears only
# '*'. Never '': matching the cleared state would send a second close.
if lane == "in_answered":
    if op is not None:
        park()
    answered = any(isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("origin") == "assistant"
                   for m in (d.get("messages") or []))
    session = str(hop.get("session_id", "") or ctx.get("session_id", "") or "")
    if not answered or not session:
        park()
    turn_id = str(ctx.get("turn_id", "") or "")
    owed = {"in": [turn_id, "*"]} if turn_id else "*"
    emit([store_bundle([
        ("ack-sealed", {"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                        "set": {"owed_turn": ""},
                        "where": {"session_id": session, "owed_turn": owed, "closed": 1}}),
        ("ack-open", {"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                      "set": {"owed_turn": ""},
                      "where": {"session_id": session, "owed_turn": owed, "closed": 0}}),
        ("ack-row", {"operation": "select", "table": "sessions",
                     "columns": ["channel", "audience_set"],
                     "where": {"session_id": session}})], "ack", session)])

if lane:
    park()

# =================================================================== PHASES
if phase == "look" and op == "select" and not err:
    rows = rows_of(d)
    try:
        keep = json.loads(str(ctx.get("keeper_body", "") or "{}"))
    except Exception:
        keep = {}
    if not isinstance(keep, dict):
        keep = {}
    keep.setdefault("messages", [])
    # One generation per channel AND round (ADR-0002 E8, GH #940). The newest
    # open row of THIS turn's round is the running generation. Every open row
    # of ANOTHER round is sealed -- the round changed, so its generation is
    # over -- and its close carries the round it was opened in. A turn without
    # a round seals no generation of another round: it is not evidence that the round changed, only
    # that its door declared none, and it runs in the round-less generation of
    # the channel. A round-less row is likewise never sealed by a turn that
    # has a round; the night closes it.
    #
    # Old duplicates heal here too (GH #954, review I-1): a channel that holds
    # MORE than one open generation of this turn's round -- the race before
    # the open became a claim left such pairs behind -- runs on in the newest
    # (rows arrive `opened_at desc`), and every older one is sealed exactly as
    # a generation of another round is, its close under its own round. That
    # holds for the round-less line of a channel as well.
    out, sid, sealed = [], "", 0
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        rsid = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
        if not rsid:
            continue
        rround = canonical_round(r.get("audience_set"))
        if rround == ROUND and not sid:
            sid = rsid
        elif rround == ROUND or (ROUND and rround):
            # One bundle per generation (GH #953): `seal-done` / `seal-owed`,
            # see `seal_legs`. Only the leg that flips `closed` 0 -> 1 decides
            # what follows, so a second turn of the new round arriving in the
            # same instant seals nothing twice. The stamp is distinct per row
            # of this run (`seal_stamp`, GH #954).
            out.append(store_bundle(seal_legs(rsid, seal_stamp(sealed)), "seal",
                                    rsid, "", str(r.get("audience_set") or "")))
            sealed += 1
    if sid:
        # The call is still running: same generation, the idle clock restarts,
        # and the generation now owes this turn's final answer (GH #953).
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "sessions",
                             "set": {"last_seen": now, "owed_turn": OWED},
                             "where": {"session_id": sid, "closed": 0}}, "touch", sid))
    else:
        # Lazy reopening: nothing pre-creates a session, THIS turn opens the
        # next generation of the channel. The id is the channel and the
        # opening instant to the microsecond; a generation sealed by this very
        # turn was opened by an EARLIER turn, so the two ids never meet.
        #
        # The turn does NOT leave with the open (GH #954): the open is a
        # claim of the round under the unique index `sessions_open_round`,
        # and only its own reply says whether this turn runs in the
        # generation it minted or in the one a racing turn opened first.
        sid = channel + "-" + now
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "sessions",
                             "row": {"channel": channel, "session_id": sid,
                                     "opened_at": now, "last_seen": now,
                                     "closed": 0, "closed_at": "",
                                     "audience_set": audience,
                                     "owed_turn": OWED}}, "open", sid,
                            json.dumps(keep)))
        emit(out)
    # `turn_id` travels ON: the id is the channel's, the session id is this
    # cell's, and the turn now carries both. `update(keep)` merges the BODY of
    # the parked turn, never a header, which is why the id has to be written in
    # here rather than ridden in with it.
    turn = {"header": {"route": "turn", "phase": "", "channel": channel,
                       "session_id": sid, "turn_id": turn_id}}
    turn.update(keep)
    out.append(turn)
    emit(out)

if phase == "open" and op == "insert" and not err:
    # The claim stands: this turn opened the generation of its round.
    if int(hop.get("rows_affected", 0) or 0) < 1:
        # Review M-3: an insert the store answered without an error and
        # without a row is not a claim lost -- that is `unique_violation`,
        # handled above -- and parking here swallowed the turn whole: no
        # answer, no reject, nothing in any log. The turn runs on under the
        # id it minted and the reject says that the row is missing.
        emit([held_turn(str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or "")),
              refused("open", op, "no_row",
                      "the insert came back WITHOUT a row and without an error. "
                      "The turn was handed on beside this reject, carrying "
                      "session id '" + str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or "")
                      + "', whose ROW was never written; the next turn on this "
                      "channel opens another generation")])
    emit([held_turn(str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or ""))])

if phase == "seal" and op == "bundle" and not err:
    # The two legs of `seal_legs`. A refused leg is a refusal of the seal, said
    # as one -- a refused leg reports rows_affected 0 and would otherwise read
    # as the lost race below.
    bad = leg_error(d, ["seal-done", "seal-owed"])
    if bad:
        emit([refused("seal", "update", bad[1], SEAL_REFUSED)])
    session = str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or "")
    if int(leg_result(d, "seal-done").get("rows_affected", 0) or 0) >= 1:
        # The generation owed no answer: it is over now. The same `close` the
        # night sweep sends (close/seal), with the round it was OPENED in --
        # never the round of the turn that ended it, which is in context here
        # and must not leave on this message as the round of that generation.
        emit([close_of(session, channel, str(ctx.get("keeper_audience", "") or ""))])
    # `seal-owed` took it (the generation still waits for the final answer of
    # its last turn: that answer's `in_answered` sends the close, GH #953), or
    # neither did -- somebody sealed it first, a parallel turn of the new round
    # or the night, and their `close` is the one; a second would hand the same
    # generation over twice.
    park()

if phase == "ack" and op == "bundle" and not err:
    bad = leg_error(d, ["ack-sealed", "ack-open", "ack-row"])
    if bad:
        emit([refused("ack", leg_result(d, bad[0]).get("operation") or "update",
                      bad[1], ACK_REFUSED)])
    if int(leg_result(d, "ack-sealed").get("rows_affected", 0) or 0) < 1:
        # The generation is still open (`ack-open` cleared the mark, the call
        # goes on), or the mark belongs to a later turn, or the night released
        # it first and sent the close itself.
        park()
    row = next((r for r in leg_rows(d, "ack-row") if isinstance(r, dict)), {})
    # The answer is on the wall; the generation sealed while it waited is over.
    # Room and round come off the row, as the night reads them.
    emit([close_of(str(ctx.get("keeper_session", "") or ""),
                   str(row.get("channel") or ""), str(row.get("audience_set") or ""))])

park()

audience_set.description: GH #940 (ADR-0002 E8): on `kstore` the round of the generation a `seal` ends (empty otherwise); on `close` the round that generation was OPENED in -- never the round of the turn that ended it.

description.purpose: The stamp in the ingress path: it gives every inbound turn the id of the generation its channel is currently in, and it restarts that channel's idle clock. One lookup, one write, and the turn travels on -- everything downstream only reads the id.
description.use_when: Between the inbound surface and the context assembly, wherever a conversation needs a beginning and an end rather than an endless thread. Wire the ingress edge into this cell and the 'turn' exit onward to the collector.
description.not_in_scope: No context assembly, no conversation content, no judgement. It does not decide when a session ends (that is the close pass) and it never deletes a generation.
description.emits_meaning: route kstore: the store ops of the current step (hop.phase carries the step, hop.channel the identity, hop.keeper_body the turn in transit -- all promoted to context by the hive edge). route turn: the inbound turn, unchanged, with hop.session_id set to the generation it belongs to. route close: a generation is over -- hop.session_id names it, hop.channel the room and hop.audience_set the round it was OPENED in. Since GH #953 a generation sealed by a turn of a new round while its last turn still WAITED for its final answer (`owed_turn` set) is not closed at the seal: the close leaves on that answer's acknowledgement (`in_answered`), after the answer is on the wall. route reject: the session store refused an op of this chain (hop.reject_reason 'store_refused', hop.store_error the store's own error_code -- a free string, because the store's code list is open -- and hop.store_operation the refused op). The body names the STEP that was refused, because the three do not leave the same thing standing: at 'look' the turn is not handed on at all (a turn without a generation is worse than a turn that stops here); at 'touch' the stamped turn ALREADY left in the same emission and what is missing is the restarted idle clock; at 'open' the turn waited for its insert (GH #954) and leaves beside the reject, and what is missing is the session ROW, which makes the next turn open yet another generation. The open's own `unique_violation` is no refusal: it is the claim of the round (`sessions_open_round`) lost to a racing first turn, and the stamp looks again and stamps the turn with the winner's generation. An insert answered WITHOUT an error and without a row (review M-3) hands the turn on beside a reject whose hop.store_error is 'no_row' -- it used to be parked, and the turn vanished without a word. A seal or an acknowledgement is a bundle (GH #295): a refused LEG is a reject as well, though the reply's header carries no error_code for it.
description.consumes_meaning: Two entry lanes, named by hop.route on the port edge. in_turn: context.channel names the identity the session belongs to and context.audience_set the round it is spoken in -- both are read only when a generation is OPENED, because both are constants of it. in_answered (GH #953): the parent's `turn_write` of the curator, one message per participant turn; only a message carrying an origin 'assistant' turn (the final answer) acts, its generation is hop.session_id (context.session_id as fallback) and the turn it answers is context.turn_id -- the CHANNEL's turn id, never hop.turn_id, which on turn_write is the episode id. A turn that arrives on in_turn without context.turn_id gets one minted here (`keeper:<trace id>:<instant>`, GH #953 R-1), so every turn owes its answer under a mark of its own; '*' is only the fallback of a store reply that carries no id, acknowledged by an answer without one. Store replies are dispatched by context.ses_phase together with hop.operation ('bundle' for the seal and the acknowledgement, whose legs are read off body.results[] and the tool_result turns by tool_call_id).
examples: in_turn on channel tg:42 with an open generation -> update last_seen + the turn with hop.session_id = tg:42-<opened_at>

in_turn on a channel whose last generation is closed -> insert a fresh row, and on its reply the turn with a NEW session_id: reopening is lazy, nothing pre-creates a session, and the insert is the claim of the round (GH #954)
in_turn on a channel whose door declares context.audience_set -> the new generation's row keeps that round, and the night that seals the generation months later still knows who was there
two first turns of round B together -> both insert, one meets unique_violation on sessions_open_round, looks again and runs in the generation the other opened

in_turn of round B while round A's generation waits for the answer of its last turn -> the seal bundle's `seal-owed` leg takes the row, no close yet; the answer's in_answered clears `owed_turn` (`ack-sealed` rows 1) and sends the close of A under round A, after the answer is on the wall
in_turn of round B while round A's generation owes nothing -> `seal-done` takes the row and the close of A leaves at once

in_turn on a channel holding two open generations of the turn's own round (left by the race before the claim) -> the newer one runs on, the older one is sealed with its own distinct stamp and closed under its own round (GH #954)
